questions.question: Which prefix length matches only a single IPv4 destination in a route table?
questions.explanation: A /32 fixes every bit and matches exactly one address.

questions.question: How many assignable endpoints does a conventional /30 provide?
questions.explanation: A /30 has four addresses, including a network and broadcast address.

questions.question: Which pair can be assigned to both routers on 192.0.2.36/31 when both support RFC 3021?
questions.explanation: Both addresses in the two-address block are endpoints on an RFC 3021 point-to-point link.

questions.question: A small Ethernet segment needs three assignable addresses and ordinary broadcast semantics. Which is the longest prefix that works?
questions.explanation: A /29 provides six assignable addresses. A /30 provides only two, and /31 and /32 do not meet the segment requirements.

questions.question: What is the role of the all-ones host value on an RFC 3021 point-to-point /31?

options.A: It marks the network and cannot be assigned
options.B: It must remain reserved as directed broadcast
options.D: It designates a third management address

questions.explanation: RFC 3021 allows both bit values as endpoint addresses and removes the need for a directed broadcast on that link.

questions.question: A designer proposes a /31 for a shared LAN requiring a router and four hosts. What rules it out?

options.A: The prefix has four addresses and must reserve two of them
options.B: The prefix requires four hosts before it can be enabled
options.C: The prefix consumes eight addresses and overlaps the entire /29
options.D: The prefix only has two addresses and the endpoint convention is for point-to-point links

questions.explanation: A /31 is useful for a supported two-endpoint link and cannot number five interfaces.

questions.question: A peer is 203.0.113.53/31. Which address belongs on the other end of its RFC 3021 link?
questions.explanation: A /31 starts on an even final octet. Odd .53 pairs with the preceding even .52.

questions.question: An old /30 link uses 198.51.100.97 and .98 as endpoints. Why can those addresses not both be kept when moving to one /31?

options.A: Both addresses are broadcasts in their respective /31s
options.B: They lie in different aligned /31 pairs
options.D: A /31 cannot use any addresses from the old /30

questions.explanation: .97 belongs with .96 and .98 belongs with .99. At least one endpoint must be renumbered.

questions.question: How many addresses are saved by assigning eight point-to-point links /31s instead of /30s?
questions.explanation: Each /31 uses two total addresses versus four for a /30. Eight links save 8 × 2 addresses.

questions.question: A neighbor at 192.0.2.3 is on the directly connected 192.0.2.0/29 transit link. Which IOS command sends traffic for only 203.0.113.42 through that neighbor?
questions.explanation: The all-ones mask installs a host route. Longer address ranges are matched by the /31, /30, and /24 alternatives.
